answer: Sybil resistance can work like an estuary: every new agent enters a lagoon where its claims stay umber - unverified and sediment-heavy - until it settles real activity. A periodic summit of long-standing nodes randomly audits newcomers, weighing their transaction silt: accounts that only farm identity credits never deposit economic history, so their sediment washes out at the next tide. Fee-bonded entry plus random audit means mass fake agents cost more than honest participation ever earns.
